rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Same-cwd recovery defaults to `--resume`, not `new`.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 176 (Push-back moves) and line 225 (Per-phase failure table) both give the same Connections-blocker push: 'student walks in without the M4 artefact accessible (closed laptop, ran out of credit, repo state unclear)... Open a fresh Claude Code session in the repo and ask it to read what the M4 run touched.' This fires BEFORE the worktree fork (§7b's cross-cwd boundary is a later section, lines 48-56), so the student is still in the same cwd as the M4 session — the case §7c says should default to `claude --resume <session-id>`, reserving `new` for cross-cwd boundaries or genuine context-contamination. None of the three named triggers (closed laptop, low credit, unclear repo state) is 'prior session's context IS the contamination' — they are interruptions, not reasons to discard the session. The harm is concrete and new as of this diff: `## Say what done-done means` (lines 26-38, new) is built around the SAME M4 session staying live — maintainer line 124 states the trick is 'the transcript inspects itself... with the original context still live', and the fence's own lead-in (line 30) reads 'This one runs in the session you sent off. Its answer lands in the transcript you are about to read.' The prompt itself (`curriculum/prompts/ae101-m5-done-done.md`) asks Claude to 'Answer per point, with evidence from this session.' A student who follows the given push instead opens an unrelated fresh session; the fresh session has no 'this session' to report evidence from, so it either refuses or (more likely, per the exact self-report failure mode this module's own Phase 1 later teaches students to distrust) produces a plausible-sounding but fabricated per-point answer, and `diagnose-and-resend` never sees a real self-audit in the M4 transcript it reads. Prework (line 8, unchanged by this diff) explicitly pre-authorizes the triggering condition — 'Walk in with your un-packaged session. Stopped, finished, ran out of credit, doesn't matter' — without naming any different recovery for the done-done beat, so every student in that pre-authorized state hits this exact gap. No maintainer accept-note anywhere in the file addresses session-resume (grepped 'resume' — zero hits).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Lead the Connections-blocker push with `claude --resume <the M4 session>` for the same-cwd case (both occurrences, line 176 and the table row at line 225); reserve the fresh-session-plus-scrollback-read fallback for when resume is genuinely unavailable, and note there that a fresh session can't answer the done-done prompt's 'evidence from this session' clause — that beat needs to run before or skip if the session is truly gone.
